A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HiF-VLA work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary sections are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LIBERO and CALVIN evaluations, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and real-world robot experiments, including supplementary results and failure cases.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds hyperparameter and architectural ablations in supplementary Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 6 retain the same motion-vector encoding, hindsight encoder, hindsight-modulated joint expert, parallel predictions, and training losses. The new state, flow, and attention variants are experimental controls, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover all four LIBERO suites, CALVIN ABC-D, and the same three real-world manipulation tasks. The added ablations vary model configurations within existing coverage rather than introduce new tasks or environments.

E2.justification: v2 adds 4D-VLA to the comprehensive LIBERO comparison in Table 4. The existing comparator rows there and the comparator sets in Tables 1–3 are retained.

E3.justification: The added experiments test expert depths of 2, 4, 6, and 8; hindsight/foresight lengths of (8,8), (8,16), and (16,16); and representation, attention, and token-order controls. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, training budgets, and primary evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component, history-length, embedding-location, loss-weight, and action-branch analyses, v2 adds substantial controls testing expert depth, temporal horizons, motion versus proprioceptive state, bidirectional versus causal attention, token ordering, and optical flow versus codec motion vectors. These directly investigate several previously untested explanations for the method's behavior.

E5.justification: The reported averaging practices, including 100 inference runs for latency and 20 real-world trials per task, are retained. v2 adds no seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 add substantial findings: six-layer expert depth performs best; longer foresight reduces success; state-only conditioning/prediction yields 92.0% versus 94.4% for motion; causal attention yields 87.4%; and optical flow yields 94.2%. Section 8.3 adds four-frame flow/MV latencies of 186.8/121.6 ms, and Table 4 adds 4D-VLA scores. These are newly reported comparisons; existing headline benchmark and real-world scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–7 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs; the new explanations of attention and temporal horizons are qualitative interpretations.

C1.justification: The three stated contributions and the claims about bidirectional temporal reasoning, efficient inference, and manipulation performance are retained. The added 'motion-centric world model' terminology reframes the already claimed prediction of future dynamics without changing the substantive capability claims.

C2.justification: Sections 8.2–8.3 add interpretations involving long-horizon error accumulation, visual interaction information beyond proprioception, and the importance of joint modeling rather than a particular motion signal. The existing limitations concerning motion-estimation noise and spatial/3D perception remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 identifies RAFT as the optical-flow estimator and describes the causal-attention control. Table 5 explicitly labels the multi-view setting and marks default configurations. Existing implementation details, hardware, training budgets, and project/code access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to RAFT, 4D-VLA, and 'World action models are zero-shot policies,' explicitly connecting HiF-VLA to World Action Models in the introduction. The existing related-work discussion and comparison with video-generation VLAs remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction receive localized world-model framing; author affiliation/contribution notes change; and acknowledgements are added. Supplementary Section 8.2 is expanded and renamed, a new Section 8.3 is inserted, and the former Section 8.3 becomes 8.4. Most existing prose and the overall organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 5 becomes a grouped ablation table, Table 6 is added, and Table 4 gains a comparator row. Table 2 is reformatted into one column, Table 1 and Figure 7 are relocated, and selected figure sizing and annotations change. The principal diagrams, rollout images, and failure-case displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The added Tables 5–6 strengthen the justification for design choices beyond v1's existing ablations, especially through state, causal-attention, and optical-flow controls. This improves explanatory support while retaining the original empirical evidence. The gain is limited: uncertainty reporting is unchanged, so small differences such as 94.2% versus 94.4% do not establish reliable equivalence or superiority.
